findings.evidence: Residue.lean:121 defines `normResidue` under only fields/algebra, while Mathlib `RingTheory/Norm/Defs.lean:76` proves `Algebra.norm_eq_one_of_not_module_finite`; the needed guarantee exists only as `Place.finiteDimensional_residueField (hF : IsFunctionField k F)` at Degree.lean:203. Eval.lean:183 calls its product “textbook” with only `IsUnitAtSupport`, which supplies no finiteness.
findings.fix: Require `Module.Finite k P.ResidueField` in the local meaningful API, or parameterize the canonical divisor evaluation by `hF : IsFunctionField k F` and use `P.finiteDimensional_residueField hF`; keep any unconstrained raw construction distinctly named and outside the claimed classical interface.
findings.issue: `normResidue` has no residue-finiteness or `IsFunctionField` argument, and consequently `normResidueOrOne` (line 136), `Divisor.evalHom` (Eval.lean:112), and `Divisor.eval` (Eval.lean:117) expose purported divisor evaluation where every non-finite residue extension is silently evaluated as `1`. Admissibility only asserts order zero, so it does not exclude this junk regime.

summary: The exported evaluation remains semantically unconstrained and can silently replace genuine residue norms by the junk value `1` outside function fields.
